solution_overview:
A certification board compared pass rates between two exam formats. There were $N_O = 4500$ candidates who took the exam online and $N_I = 7500$ candidates who took the exam in person. Among these, $F_O = 810$ online candidates failed and $F_I = 600$ in-person candidates failed.

We model the probabilities by selecting one exam record at random from the combined pool of all candidates. The total number of candidates is the sum of those who took the exam online and in person:

$$N_{\text{total}} = N_O + N_I = 4500 + 7500 = 12000$$

The total number of candidates who failed is the sum of online failures and in-person failures:

$$F_{\text{total}} = F_O + F_I = 810 + 600 = 1410$$

The number of candidates who passed online is:

$$P_O = N_O - F_O = 4500 - 810 = 3690$$

The number of candidates who passed in person is:

$$P_I = N_I - F_I = 7500 - 600 = 6900$$

So the total number of candidates who passed is:

$$P_{\text{total}} = P_O + P_I = 3690 + 6900 = 10590$$

As a check, $P_{\text{total}} + F_{\text{total}} = 10590 + 1410 = 12000 = N_{\text{total}}$, which is consistent.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The probability that a randomly selected candidate failed is the ratio of the total number of failures to the total number of candidates.

$$P(\text{failed}) = \frac{F_{\text{total}}}{N_{\text{total}}}$$

$$P(\text{failed}) = \frac{1410}{12000}$$

$$P(\text{failed}) = 0.1175 = 11.75\%$$

Since $11.75\% > 11.5\%$, the statement is True.

**B.** → True

The probability that a candidate failed given they took the exam online is a conditional probability. This is the ratio of online failures to the total number of online candidates.

$$P(\text{failed} \mid \text{online}) = \frac{F_O}{N_O}$$

$$P(\text{failed} \mid \text{online}) = \frac{810}{4500}$$

$$P(\text{failed} \mid \text{online}) = 0.18 = 18\%$$

Since $18\% > 17\%$, the statement is True.

**C.** → True

The probability that a failing candidate took the exam online is a conditional probability. This is the ratio of online failures to the total number of failures.

$$P(\text{online} \mid \text{failed}) = \frac{F_O}{F_{\text{total}}}$$

$$P(\text{online} \mid \text{failed}) = \frac{810}{1410}$$

$$P(\text{online} \mid \text{failed}) \approx 0.574468 \approx 57.45\%$$

Since $57.45\% > 57\%$, the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The probability that a failing candidate took the exam in person is a conditional probability. This is the ratio of in-person failures to the total number of failures.

$$P(\text{in person} \mid \text{failed}) = \frac{F_I}{F_{\text{total}}}$$

$$P(\text{in person} \mid \text{failed}) = \frac{600}{1410}$$

$$P(\text{in person} \mid \text{failed}) \approx 0.425532 \approx 42.55\%$$

Since $42.55\% > 40\%$, the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The probability that a candidate passed is the complement of the probability that a candidate failed.

$$P(\text{passed}) = 1 - P(\text{failed})$$

Using the result from Statement A:

$$P(\text{passed}) = 1 - 0.1175$$

$$P(\text{passed}) = 0.8825 = 88.25\%$$

Alternatively, we can calculate this directly from the total number of passed candidates:

$$P(\text{passed}) = \frac{P_{\text{total}}}{N_{\text{total}}} = \frac{10590}{12000} = 0.8825 = 88.25\%$$

Since $88.25\% > 87\%$, the statement is True.
